entities.name: CBS Records
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
CBS Records, the recorded music division of CBS Corporation operating under that name from 1938 through its 1988 acquisition by Sony (becoming Sony Music Entertainment), was one of the most important record labels in 20th-century American music history — encompassing Columbia Records, Epic Records, and other imprints — and home to Bob Dylan, Barbra Streisand, Michael Jackson, Bruce Springsteen, Billy Joel, Julio Iglesias, and dozens of other major artists, making it the 20th century's most commercially successful recorded music company at its peak.

CBS's recorded music roots trace to the Columbia Phonograph Company (founded 1887), which CBS acquired in 1938. Under this ownership, Columbia Records expanded into one of America's dominant labels. CBS Records as an entity was formally named in 1974, incorporating Columbia Records (the flagship US label), Epic Records (second label targeting different markets), Portrait, ARC, and other imprints. The combination of Columbia's prestige roster (Dylan, Springsteen) with Epic's Michael Jackson relationship (Jackson moved to Epic from Motown's parent in 1975) made CBS Records the world's most commercially powerful music company in the 1970s-1980s.

Michael Jackson's CBS/Epic recordings — Off the Wall (1979), Thriller (1982, the best-selling album in recorded music history at 66+ million copies), and Bad (1987) — represent the commercial apex of any record company's roster. CBS sold the records division to Sony in 1988 for $2 billion, creating Sony Music Entertainment and ending CBS's music presence. The sale was described as part of Japan's cultural acquisition of American entertainment assets, marking a significant transformation in the music industry's corporate ownership.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: CBS Records — the parent of Columbia and Epic, home to Thriller (best-selling album in history) and the most commercially successful record company roster of the 20th century, and whose 1988 Sony sale transformed the music industry's corporate ownership landscape — is one of recorded music's most historically significant institutions.
